prompt: The front of a tent is an isosceles triangle: the two slanted edges are each $13$ ft and the floor is $10$ ft wide. How tall is the tent at its peak, in feet?
hint: Drop the height from the peak straight down to the floor — it splits the isosceles triangle into two identical right triangles.

hints.text: Drop the height from the peak straight down to the floor — it splits the isosceles triangle into two identical right triangles.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up on a $5$-$5$-$6$ triangle: half the base is $3$, so $3^2 + h^2 = 5^2$ gives $h = 4$. Same two moves here — halve the floor width, then use the Pythagorean theorem.
That height hits the middle of the floor, so each small triangle has a leg of $10 \div 2 = 5$ and hypotenuse $13$.

explanation: The height of an isosceles triangle drawn to the base cuts the base exactly in half.
That creates a right triangle with hypotenuse $13$ (the slanted edge) and one leg $5$ (half of $10$).
Solve: $h^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$, so the peak is $h = 12$ ft high.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two triangles, one answer
steps: Both halves are congruent right triangles, so you only need to solve one of them.
Each is a $5$-$12$-$13$ triple — a family worth memorizing alongside $3$-$4$-$5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The tempting wrong answer is $\sqrt{169 - 100} = \sqrt{69} \approx 8.3$: using the WHOLE $10$-ft floor as a leg. But the full floor is not a leg of either right triangle — the height lands in the middle of it.
Before squaring anything, redraw the picture with the height in place and label the halved base. Half of $10$ is $5$, and $13^2 - 5^2$ gives the clean $12$.
